# Introduction

This laboratory aims to **develop and evaluate an AI model** for predicting patient outcomes in the *AIDS Clinical Trial Group Study 175* dataset.  
The goal is to design a **Trustworthy Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)** by separating the training and evaluation of the AI model from its user interface.

The Dataset can be found here: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/890/aids+clinical+trials+group+study+175.

Specifically, in this R Markdown we will:

- **Inspect** correlation
- **Balance** the target
- **Train** a logistic regression classifier to predict patient death based on key clinical variables.  
- **Perform** a proper model evaluation including ROC, Precision–Recall, and Calibration Curves.  
- **Compute** key performance metrics such as **AUC**, **Precision**, **Recall**, **F1-score**, and **Brier score**.  
- **Investigate** fairness metrics such as **Proportional Parity**, and **Equalized Odds**.
- **Save** the trained model and evaluation data into an `.RData` file for later use in the **Shiny-based CDSS** interface.

``` {r load-data, include = FALSE}
data_path <- "AIDS_ClinicalTrial_GroupStudy175.csv"
df_orig <- readr::read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Crea la variabile target (1 = death, 0 = alive)
df_preprocessed <- df_orig %>%
  mutate(target = as.factor(as.integer(label))) %>%
  #mutate(target = as.integer(label)) %>%     # target = outcome
  mutate(trt = factor(trt)) %>%              # treatment = feature
  mutate_if(is.character, as.factor)

# Seleziona predittori e target
predictors <- c("age", "wtkg", "hemo", "cd40", "cd420", "trt")
df <- df_preprocessed %>% select(all_of(c(predictors, "target"))) %>% na.omit()
```

### Correlation Analysis

```{r, echo=FALSE}
library(corrplot)
cor_matrix <- cor(df_orig, use = "complete.obs")
corrplot(cor_matrix, method = "color", type = "upper",
         tl.col = "black", tl.srt = 45)
```

Based on these findings and medical knowledge we decide to use "age", "wtkg", "hemo", "cd40", "cd420", and "trt" as predictor variables.

### Class Balance

Baseline Class Balance in the dataset.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# plot class balance
ggplot(df, aes(x = factor(target), fill = factor(target))) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(stat = "count", aes(label = ..count..), vjust = -0.3, size = 5) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("0" = "Alive", "1" = "Death")) +
  labs(
    title = "Class Balance in AIDS Clinical Trial Study 175",
    x = "Outcome",
    y = "Number of Patients"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```

Because of this big class imbalance we decided to employ Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) to rebalance.

Class Balance after using SMOTE:

```{r smote_balancing, echo=FALSE}
# Do balancing with SMOTE

# Recipe: dummy-encode before SMOTE
rec <- recipe(target ~ ., data = df) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%  # convert trt → numeric dummy vars
  step_smote(target, over_ratio = 1)        # apply SMOTE

# Apply the recipe
df_smote <- prep(rec) %>% bake(new_data = NULL)
df <- df_smote

df$target <- as.integer(df$target)
df$target <- df$target - 1
df$target <- factor(df$target)

df$trt <- as.integer(df$trt_X1 * 1 + df$trt_X2 * 2 + df$trt_X3 * 3 + 0)

df <- df %>% select(-trt_X1, -trt_X2, -trt_X3)

df$trt <- factor(df$trt)
```

``` {r split, include = FALSE}
trainIndex <- createDataPartition(df$target, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
train <- df[trainIndex, ]
test  <- df[-trainIndex, ]
# Check class balance
table(train$target)
table(test$target)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# plot class balance
ggplot(df, aes(x = factor(target), fill = factor(target))) +
  geom_bar(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(stat = "count", aes(label = ..count..), vjust = -0.3, size = 5) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("0" = "Alive", "1" = "Death")) +
  labs(
    title = "Class Balance in AIDS Clinical Trial Study 175",
    x = "Outcome",
    y = "Number of Patients"
  ) +
```


# Model Performance Metrics

With the balanced dataset and the selected variables we train a logistic regression model. The model performance metrics are summarized below.

```{r metrics, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
library(glue)

# --- Predizioni ---
pred_prob <- predict(model_logit, newdata = test, type = "prob")[, "1"]
pred_class <- ifelse(pred_prob >= 0.5, 1, 0)

# --- Confusion Matrix ---
cm <- confusionMatrix(factor(pred_class, levels=c("0","1")), test$target, positive = "1")

# --- Trasforma in tabella leggibile ---
cm_table <- as.data.frame.matrix(cm$table)
colnames(cm_table) <- paste("Actual", colnames(cm_table))
rownames(cm_table) <- paste("Predicted", rownames(cm_table))

# --- ROC e altre metriche ---
roc_obj <- roc(as.numeric(test$target) - 1, as.numeric(pred_prob) - 1)
auc_val <- auc(roc_obj)
precision <- Precision(test$target, pred_class)
recall <- Recall(test$target, pred_class)
f1 <- F1_Score(test$target, pred_class)

# --- Threshold ottimale (Youden Index) ---
coords <- coords(
  roc_obj,
  "best",
  ret = c("threshold", "sensitivity", "specificity"),
  best.method = "youden"
)

# --- Riepilogo metriche ---
metrics <- data.frame(
  Accuracy = round(cm$overall["Accuracy"], 3),
  Precision = round(precision, 3),
  Recall = round(recall, 3),
  F1_Score = round(f1, 3),
  Sensitivity = round(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 3),
  Specificity = round(cm$byClass["Specificity"], 3),
  AUC = round(auc_val, 3)
)

# --- Mostra la Confusion Matrix con stile coerente ---
knitr::kable(cm_table, caption = "<span style='white-space: nowrap;'>Confusion Matrix (Predicted vs. Actual)</span>", digits = 0, align = "c") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position = "left",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )

# --- Tabella ordinata ---
knitr::kable(metrics, caption = "Model Performance Metrics", digits = 3) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "left",
                            bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"))
```

# Calibration curve

```{r calibration-curve, fig.height=5.5, fig.width=8}
# --- Calibration Curve (Reliability Plot) with metrics ---

# Divide le probabilità predette in 10 bin (decili)
cal_df <- data.frame(
  pred_prob = pred_prob,
  true = as.numeric(test$target)-1
) %>%
  mutate(bin = ntile(pred_prob, 10)) %>%
  group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pred = mean(pred_prob),
    obs_rate = mean(true)
  )

# --- Metriche di calibrazione ---
# 1. Brier Score (errore medio quadratico)
brier_score <- mean((pred_prob - (as.numeric(test$target)-1))^2)

# 2. Calibrazione lineare: true ~ predicted
cal_model <- glm(true ~ pred_prob, data = data.frame(true = as.numeric(test$target)-1, pred_prob = pred_prob), family = binomial())
cal_intercept <- coef(cal_model)[1]
cal_slope <- coef(cal_model)[2]

# --- Plot Calibration Curve ---
ggplot(cal_df, aes(x = mean_pred, y = obs_rate)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#E41A1C") +
  geom_line(color = "#E41A1C", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray40") +
  labs(
    title = "Calibration Curve (AIDS Study)",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Brier Score = ", round(brier_score, 3),
      " | Intercept = ", round(cal_intercept, 2),
      " | Slope = ", round(cal_slope, 2)
    ),
    x = "Predicted probability of death",
    y = "Observed frequency of death"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.7, y = 0.15, label = "Perfect calibration", color = "gray40", size = 4)
```

```{r fairness metric, include=TRUE}
compute_fairness_metrics <- function(data, group_var,
                                     prob_col = "pred_prob",
                                     true_col = "target",
                                     pred_col = "pred_class") {
  
  groups <- levels(as.factor(data[[group_var]]))
  
  results <- lapply(groups, function(g) {
    df <- data[data[[group_var]] == g, ]
    
    y_true <- as.numeric(as.character(df[[true_col]]))
    y_pred <- df[[pred_col]]
    
    TP <- sum(y_true == 1 & y_pred == 1)
    FN <- sum(y_true == 1 & y_pred == 0)
    FP <- sum(y_true == 0 & y_pred == 1)
    TN <- sum(y_true == 0 & y_pred == 0)
    
    demographic_parity <- mean(y_pred == 1)
    TPR <- ifelse((TP + FN) > 0, TP / (TP + FN), NA)
    FPR <- ifelse((FP + TN) > 0, FP / (FP + TN), NA)
    
    data.frame(
      group = g,
      demographic_parity = demographic_parity,
      TPR = TPR,
      FPR = FPR
    )
  })
  
  do.call(rbind, results)
}
```

# Calibration Improvement

We also investigated influence of post-hoc calibration improvement measures as in the study.


```{r nested-cv-calibration-full, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=5.5, results='asis'}
# =====================================================
# 1) HELPERS
# =====================================================
eps <- 1e-6
clamp <- function(p) pmin(pmax(as.numeric(p), eps), 1 - eps)

brier <- function(y, p) mean((clamp(p) - y)^2)

logloss <- function(y, p) {
  p <- clamp(p)
  -mean(y * log(p) + (1 - y) * log(1 - p))
}

ece <- function(y, p, n_bins = 10) {
  p <- clamp(p)
  bins <- cut(p, breaks = seq(0,1,length.out=n_bins+1), include.lowest=TRUE)
  tibble(y=y, p=p, bin=bins) %>%
    group_by(bin) %>%
    summarise(acc=mean(y), conf=mean(p), n=n(), .groups="drop") %>%
    mutate(w=n/sum(n)) %>%
    summarise(sum(w * abs(acc-conf))) %>% pull()
}

reliability_df <- function(y, p, n_bins=10) {
  d <- tibble(y=as.numeric(y), p=clamp(p)) %>% filter(is.finite(y), is.finite(p))
  if (nrow(d) < 5) return(tibble(p_mean=numeric(0), y_rate=numeric(0), n=integer(0)))
  d %>%
    mutate(bin = ntile(p, n_bins)) %>%
    group_by(bin) %>%
    summarise(p_mean=mean(p), y_rate=mean(y), n=n(), .groups="drop") %>%
    arrange(p_mean)
}

# =====================================================
# 2) TEMPERATURE SCALING (robust)
# =====================================================
fit_temperature <- function(p_cal, y_cal) {
  p_cal <- clamp(p_cal)
  y_cal <- as.numeric(y_cal)

  nll <- function(logT) {
    T <- exp(logT)
    pT <- plogis(qlogis(p_cal) / T)
    -mean(y_cal*log(clamp(pT)) + (1-y_cal)*log(1-clamp(pT)))
  }

  opt <- optimize(nll, interval=c(log(1e-2), log(1e2)))
  exp(opt$minimum)
}

# =====================================================
# 3) CALIBRATION METHODS (robust)
# =====================================================
calibrate_all <- function(p_cal, y_cal, p_test) {

  # ensure safe probabilities everywhere
  p_cal  <- clamp(p_cal)
  p_test <- clamp(p_test)
  y_cal  <- as.numeric(y_cal)

  # Uncalibrated
  p_uncal <- p_test

  # (A) Platt scaling (robust: clamp before qlogis)
  platt_fit <- glm(y_cal ~ qlogis(p_cal), family=binomial())
  p_platt <- plogis(predict(platt_fit, newdata=data.frame(p_cal=p_test)))

  # (B) Isotonic regression (robust ordering)
  ord <- order(p_cal)
  iso <- isoreg(p_cal[ord], y_cal[ord])
  p_iso <- approx(iso$x, iso$yf, xout=p_test, rule=2, ties="ordered")$y

  # (C) Quantile binning (robust against empty bins)
  n_bins <- 10
  br <- unique(quantile(p_cal, probs=seq(0,1,length.out=n_bins+1), na.rm=TRUE))
  if (length(br) < 3) br <- unique(seq(min(p_cal), max(p_cal), length.out=n_bins+1))

  bin_tbl <- tibble(p=p_cal, y=y_cal) %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(p, breaks=br, include.lowest=TRUE, right=TRUE)) %>%
    group_by(bin) %>%
    summarise(p_min=min(p), p_max=max(p), y_rate=mean(y), .groups="drop")

  bin_apply <- function(p) {
    p <- clamp(p)
    out <- numeric(length(p))
    for (i in seq_along(p)) {
      idx <- which(p[i] >= bin_tbl$p_min & p[i] <= bin_tbl$p_max)
      if (length(idx)==0) {
        out[i] <- if (p[i] < min(bin_tbl$p_min)) bin_tbl$y_rate[which.min(bin_tbl$p_min)]
        else bin_tbl$y_rate[which.max(bin_tbl$p_max)]
      } else out[i] <- bin_tbl$y_rate[idx[1]]
    }
    clamp(out)
  }
  p_bin <- bin_apply(p_test)

  # (D) Temperature scaling
  T <- fit_temperature(p_cal, y_cal)
  p_temp <- plogis(qlogis(p_test) / T)

  list(
    uncal = clamp(p_uncal),
    platt = clamp(p_platt),
    iso   = clamp(p_iso),
    bin   = clamp(p_bin),
    temp  = clamp(p_temp)
  )
}

# =====================================================
# 4) NESTED CV
# =====================================================
K <- 5
folds <- createFolds(df$target, k=K)

pooled <- list(
  RF = list(uncal=c(), platt=c(), iso=c(), bin=c(), temp=c(), y=c()),
  GB = list(uncal=c(), platt=c(), iso=c(), bin=c(), temp=c(), y=c())
)

metrics_all <- list()

for (k in seq_along(folds)) {

  test_idx <- folds[[k]]
  train_idx <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(df)), test_idx)

  outer_train <- df[train_idx, ]
  outer_test  <- df[test_idx, ]

  inner_idx <- createDataPartition(outer_train$target, p=0.25, list=FALSE)
  fit <- outer_train[-inner_idx, ]
  cal <- outer_train[inner_idx, ]

  y_cal  <- as.numeric(as.character(cal$target))
  y_test <- as.numeric(as.character(outer_test$target))

  # ---- Random Forest
  rf <- model_logit
  p_cal_rf  <- clamp(predict(rf, cal, type="prob")[,2])
  p_test_rf <- clamp(predict(rf, outer_test, type="prob")[,2])
  cal_rf <- calibrate_all(p_cal_rf, y_cal, p_test_rf)
  
  # ---- Pool
  pooled$RF$y <- c(pooled$RF$y, y_test)

  for (m in names(cal_rf)) {
    pooled$RF[[m]] <- c(pooled$RF[[m]], cal_rf[[m]])
  }

  # ---- Metrics (per fold)
  metrics_all[[length(metrics_all)+1]] <- tibble(
    Fold=k, Model="Random Forest",
    Method=c("Uncalibrated","Platt scaling","Isotonic regression","Quantile binning","Temperature scaling"),
    ECE=c(ece(y_test, cal_rf$uncal), ece(y_test, cal_rf$platt), ece(y_test, cal_rf$iso), ece(y_test, cal_rf$bin), ece(y_test, cal_rf$temp)),
    LogLoss=c(logloss(y_test, cal_rf$uncal), logloss(y_test, cal_rf$platt), logloss(y_test, cal_rf$iso), logloss(y_test, cal_rf$bin), logloss(y_test, cal_rf$temp)),
    Brier=c(brier(y_test, cal_rf$uncal), brier(y_test, cal_rf$platt), brier(y_test, cal_rf$iso), brier(y_test, cal_rf$bin), brier(y_test, cal_rf$temp))
  )
}

metrics_df <- bind_rows(metrics_all)

# =====================================================
# 5) SUMMARY TABLE (mean ± sd)
# =====================================================
summary_tbl <- metrics_df %>%
  group_by(Model, Method) %>%
  summarise(
    ECE_mean=mean(ECE), ECE_sd=sd(ECE),
    LogLoss_mean=mean(LogLoss), LogLoss_sd=sd(LogLoss),
    Brier_mean=mean(Brier), Brier_sd=sd(Brier),
    .groups="drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    ECE = sprintf("%.3f ± %.3f", ECE_mean, ECE_sd),
    LogLoss = sprintf("%.3f ± %.3f", LogLoss_mean, LogLoss_sd),
    Brier = sprintf("%.3f ± %.3f", Brier_mean, Brier_sd)
  ) %>%
  select(Model, Method, ECE, LogLoss, Brier)


# =====================================================
# 6) FIGURE 1 — RELIABILITY (RF vs GB)
# =====================================================
make_fig1 <- function(model_key, title_txt) {
  y <- pooled[[model_key]]$y
  fig1_df <- bind_rows(
    reliability_df(y, pooled[[model_key]]$uncal, 10) %>% mutate(Method="Uncalibrated"),
    reliability_df(y, pooled[[model_key]]$platt, 10) %>% mutate(Method="Platt scaling"),
    reliability_df(y, pooled[[model_key]]$iso,   10) %>% mutate(Method="Isotonic regression"),
    reliability_df(y, pooled[[model_key]]$bin,   10) %>% mutate(Method="Quantile binning"),
    reliability_df(y, pooled[[model_key]]$temp,  10) %>% mutate(Method="Temperature scaling")
  )

  ggplot(fig1_df, aes(x=p_mean, y=y_rate, color=Method)) +
    geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="gray40") +
    geom_line(linewidth=1.05, alpha=0.95) +
    geom_point(size=2.6, alpha=0.9) +
    coord_equal(xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1)) +
    labs(title=title_txt, x="Mean predicted probability", y="Observed event rate") +
    theme_minimal(base_size=12) +
    theme(legend.position="right")
}

p1_rf <- make_fig1("RF", "Figure 1a. Reliability diagram — Random Forest (pooled CV)")

gridExtra::grid.arrange(p1_rf, ncol=1)

# =====================================================
# 7) FIGURE 2 — OVERLAID HIST (uncal vs best-by-ECE) [ROBUST]
# =====================================================

# Helper: map keys -> pretty names (1 posto solo)
model_key_to_label <- function(model_key) {
  if (model_key == "RF") return("Random Forest")
  stop("Unknown model_key: ", model_key)
}

# Compute best method per MODEL KEY using metrics_df
best_method_per_key <- metrics_df %>%
  filter(Method != "Uncalibrated") %>%
  mutate(ModelKey = ifelse(Model == "Random Forest", "RF")) %>%
  group_by(ModelKey, Method) %>%
  summarise(ECE = mean(ECE), LogLoss = mean(LogLoss), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(ModelKey) %>%
  dplyr::slice(which.min(ECE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(ModelKey, BestMethod = Method)

# robust getter (with fallback)
pick_probs <- function(model_key, method_name) {
  # fallback if empty
  if (length(method_name) == 0 || is.na(method_name)) method_name <- "Temperature scaling"

  if (method_name == "Platt scaling") return(pooled[[model_key]]$platt)
  if (method_name == "Isotonic regression") return(pooled[[model_key]]$iso)
  if (method_name == "Quantile binning") return(pooled[[model_key]]$bin)
  if (method_name == "Temperature scaling") return(pooled[[model_key]]$temp)

  # ultimate fallback
  pooled[[model_key]]$uncal
}

model_key = "RF"
binwidth = 0.05

model_label <- model_key_to_label(model_key)

p_unc  <- pooled[[model_key]]$uncal
p_iso <- pooled[[model_key]]$iso
p_platt <- pooled[[model_key]]$platt
p_bin <- pooled[[model_key]]$bin
p_temp <- pooled[[model_key]]$temp

breaks <- seq(0, 1, by = binwidth)

hist_df <- tibble(
  p = c(p_unc, p_iso, p_platt, p_bin, p_temp),
  Stage = factor(
    c(rep("Uncalibrated", length(p_unc)),
      rep("Isotonic Regression", length(p_iso)),
      rep("Platt Scaling", length(p_platt)),
      rep("Quantile Binning", length(p_bin)),
      rep("Temperature Scaling", length(p_temp))),
    levels = c("Uncalibrated", "Isotonic Regression", "Platt Scaling", "Quantile Binning", "Temperature Scaling")
  )
)


p <- ggplot() +
geom_histogram(data = filter(hist_df, Stage == "Uncalibrated"), 
               aes(x = p, fill = Stage), 
               breaks = breaks, alpha = 0.35, position = "identity") +
geom_histogram(data = filter(hist_df, Stage == "Isotonic Regression"), 
               aes(x = p, fill = Stage), 
               breaks = breaks, alpha = 0.35, position = "identity") +
geom_histogram(data = filter(hist_df, Stage == "Platt Scaling"), 
               aes(x = p, fill = Stage), 
               breaks = breaks, alpha = 0.35, position = "identity") +
geom_histogram(data = filter(hist_df, Stage == "Quantile Binning"), 
               aes(x = p, fill = Stage), 
               breaks = breaks, alpha = 0.35, position = "identity") +
geom_histogram(data = filter(hist_df, Stage == "Temperature Scaling"), 
               aes(x = p, fill = Stage), 
               breaks = breaks, alpha = 0.35, position = "identity") +
scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
labs(
  title = paste0("Probability Distribution Histogram"),
  x = "Predicted probability",
  y = "Count",
  fill = "Stage"
) +
theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# Convert to plotly — now each stage is its own trace
p_plotly <- ggplotly(p, dynamicTicks = TRUE)

enabled_stages <- c("Uncalibrated", "Platt Scaling")
disabled_stages <- c("Isotonic Regression", "Quantile Binning", "Temperature Scaling")

# Loop over traces and set visibility
for(i in seq_along(p_plotly$x$data)) {
  stage_name <- p_plotly$x$data[[i]]$name
  if(stage_name %in% enabled_stages) {
    p_plotly$x$data[[i]]$visible <- TRUE
  } else {
    p_plotly$x$data[[i]]$visible <- "legendonly"  # hide but keep in legend
  }
}

p_plotly <- p_plotly %>% layout(width = 800, height = 400)
p_plotly

knitr::kable(summary_tbl, caption="Calibration metrics across methods (nested 5-fold CV).") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width=FALSE, bootstrap_options=c("striped","hover","condensed"))
```
